# Aether

When an agent proposes a change to a running system, Aether computes what that
change actually does: branch the architecture, simulate a failure
deterministically, and keep the commit decision with a human.

## What an agent can do on this page

This page publishes WebMCP tools through `document.modelContext`. The surface is
state-aware: a committed architecture registers ten read and branch tools, an
editable canvas registers sixteen, and eighteen once a repair future exists. A
merge closes the write tools again, leaving twelve. Component
and region identifiers in those schemas are enumerated from the live graph, so a
component added moments ago can be addressed immediately.

Start with `get_architecture_summary`. It returns the components on the page,
their dependencies, the latest evidence, and the next allowed action. Every tool
result names a `nextAction`, and every rejection names the field that failed and
the values that would have worked.

## What an agent cannot do

No approve, merge, or removal tool is registered, in any state. An agent
proposes and reconfigures; only a human commits a future or reverses one. The
command layer enforces the same boundary independently of the tool list.
